The role covers civil, hydro-mechanical, and electro-mechanical works, including headworks, tunnels and waterways, powerhouse, and associated infrastructure. Key Duties and Responsibilities 1. Planning and Execution •Translate project drawings, specifications, and schedules into executable site work plans and daily and weekly targets. •Plan and coordinate the sequencing of civil works (river diversion, cofferdams, intake, desanding basins, headrace tunnel or canal, surge shaft, penstock, powerhouse, and tailrace) with hydro-mechanical and electro-mechanical installation. •Ensure timely mobilization of manpower, plant, equipment, and materials to meet the construction programme. •Monitor progress against the baseline schedule, identify slippage, and implement recovery measures. 2. Technical and Quality Management •Supervise construction methods for tunneling, drilling and blasting, concreting, grouting, dam or weir works, and slope stabilization. •Review method statements, shop drawings, and work procedures before execution. •Enforce QA/QC procedures and ensure materials testing (concrete, aggregates, reinforcement, welds) meets specifications. •Coordinate with the design team and the Engineer on site queries, design changes, and technical clarifications (RFIs). •Oversee survey control, setting-out, and as-built documentation. 3. Contract and Cost Control •Ensure works comply with contract conditions, drawings, and specifications. •Support measurement of works, interim payment certificates, and variation or claim documentation. •Control resource utilization to minimize waste and keep costs within budget. •Coordinate with contractors and subcontractors, monitoring their performance and compliance. 4. Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) •Enforce site safety standards, particularly for high-risk activities such as blasting, working at height, confined spaces in tunnels and shafts, heavy lifting, and work near water. •Ensure environmental and social safeguards are followed, including spoil disposal, sediment control, water quality, and community commitments. •Lead toolbox talks, safety audits, and incident investigation and reporting. 5. Coordination and Reporting •Liaise with the client or owner, consultants, contractors, and local authorities. •Prepare and present daily, weekly, and monthly progress reports. •Chair or attend site coordination and progress meetings. •Manage interfaces between multiple contract packages (civil, hydro-mechanical, electro-mechanical, transmission line, and access roads). 6. Team and Resource Management •Lead, mentor, and evaluate site engineering and supervisory staff. •Manage plant, equipment, fuel, and material logistics, especially given remote site conditions. •Resolve site-level disputes and workforce issues. Qualifications and Experience •Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering (Master's degree or specialization in hydropower or hydraulics preferred). •Typically 10 or more years in construction, with 5 or more years in hydropower or heavy civil / underground works, including supervisory experience. •Strong knowledge of tunneling, dam or weir construction, concrete works, and hydro-mechanical installation. •Familiarity with FIDIC contracts, project scheduling tools (Primavera P6 or MS Project), and QA/QC systems. •Professional engineering registration (e.g., NEC registration in Nepal) is usually required. Key Skills and Competencies •Leadership, planning, and problem-solving under remote and challenging site conditions. •Strong safety orientation and contract awareness. •Effective communication and stakeholder coordination. •Decision-making and the ability to work under pressure to meet deadlines. Apply at : recruiter@getjobnepal.com
